name: Manufacturing
title: Production quality containment assistant
summary: Connect quality signals, lot genealogy, and maintenance evidence before a supervisor approves containment work.
situation: Illustrative architecture: An electronics plant observes a rise in solder inspection failures after a component lot change. Engineers need to connect inspection images, feeder setup, supplier lots, and machine maintenance history while production continues. Agents assemble evidence and candidate checks; established plant controls retain equipment and release authority.
problem: Different systems use station, batch, and serial identifiers inconsistently. A model that confuses correlation with root cause can recommend unnecessarily broad containment or miss affected units. Production latency also differs from the seconds-to-minutes timescale suitable for agent analysis.
whyAgents: Genealogy, quality, maintenance, and planning specialists can inspect distinct evidence concurrently. A deterministic lineage graph defines potentially affected material, while agents formulate testable hypotheses and human engineers decide corrective action.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure evidence assembly time and completeness before claiming lower scrap or downtime. Production benefits depend on engineering response and process changes, so dashboards must separate agent preparation from physical corrective outcomes.

agents.name: Genealogy investigator
agents.responsibility: Trace components through lots, work orders, and finished serials.
agents.boundary: Cannot change traceability records or remove material holds.

agents.name: Quality evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Compare inspection patterns and retrieve representative images and measurements.
agents.boundary: Cannot declare product conformity or infer unmeasured defects.

agents.name: Maintenance analyst
agents.responsibility: Correlate calibration, alarms, and service history with affected equipment intervals.
agents.boundary: Cannot write controller settings or acknowledge safety alarms.

agents.name: Containment planner
agents.responsibility: Draft bounded inspection and material-hold proposals with affected inventory references.
agents.boundary: Supervisor approval is required for holds, rework, and production changes.

systems.name: Manufacturing execution system
systems.role: Owns work-order progress, serial genealogy, and material consumption history.

systems.name: Quality and maintenance platforms
systems.role: Provide inspection measurements, calibration versions, and approved work procedures.

systems.name: Industrial data gateway
systems.role: Exposes buffered equipment telemetry to the analysis network without a direct agent-to-controller path.

flow.title: Capture quality signal
flow.description: Register the inspection event and station context; distinguish sensor anomalies from confirmed quality observations.

flow.title: Build affected set
flow.description: Traverse exact lot and serial relationships from the manufacturing record, retaining unknown genealogy as an explicit gap.

flow.title: Compare evidence windows
flow.description: Align inspection timestamps with component changeovers, calibration records, and machine events using synchronized clocks.

flow.title: Generate hypotheses
flow.description: Specialists propose bounded explanations with supporting and contradicting evidence; do not present a ranking as proven causation.

flow.title: Review containment
flow.description: Show the supervisor the affected-set query, proposed inspections, production impact, and evidence uncertainty before any hold is authorized.

flow.title: Execute approved work
flow.description: Submit a versioned maintenance or containment work order through the existing workflow and track completion evidence separately from issue resolution.

failures.scenario: Genealogy is incomplete for a reworked batch.
failures.detection: Traversal finds consumed components without linked finished serials.
failures.recovery: Mark the affected set incomplete and ask traceability staff to resolve it before narrowing containment.

failures.scenario: A telemetry clock drifts across a changeover.
failures.detection: Time synchronization checks disagree with station event sequence.
failures.recovery: Use trusted production event ordering and label the correlation window uncertain pending clock repair.

controls: Keep industrial control credentials and safety functions outside the agent runtime.
Require supervisor approval for holds, rework, and equipment-setting changes.
Attach measurement units, calibration status, and source timestamps to quality evidence.
Separate candidate causal hypotheses from verified engineering findings.
Enforce plant and product-line permissions for supplier and production data.

metrics.name: Containment preparation time
metrics.definition: Time from confirmed quality signal to a supervisor-reviewable affected-set proposal.

metrics.name: Genealogy coverage
metrics.definition: Affected serials with complete component ancestry divided by serials in the investigation scope.

metrics.name: Hypothesis confirmation rate
metrics.definition: Reviewed hypotheses supported by engineering tests divided by hypotheses tested.

metrics.name: Work-order closure fidelity
metrics.definition: Completed actions with required inspection evidence divided by actions marked complete.

tradeoffs.benefit: Protects plant control networks from model activity.
tradeoffs.cost: Analysis may lag machine events and cannot replace real-time control.
Incomplete historical records can delay a narrow proposal.

tradeoffs.benefit: Brings quality and maintenance perspectives together.
tradeoffs.cost: Conflicting explanations require explicit engineering adjudication.

rollout.acceptance: Plant engineers verify affected-set queries and that every hypothesis is distinguished from a confirmed cause.
One line compares draft containment plans with existing investigations while all equipment access remains read only.
Supervisors accept controlled draft integration after hold permissions, duplicate events, and clock-drift recovery pass.
